ADDM Task ADDM:659179364_1_12086

          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:659179364_1_12086'
          ---------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 12085 to 12086.
Time period starts at 06-SEP-25 11.30.58 AM
Time period ends at 06-SEP-25 12.30.20 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'KRISHNA' with DB ID 659179364.
Database version during analysis period was 19.25.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance krishna, numbered 1 and hosted at
kirshnadb-pr.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 24986 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 7.01.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Soft Parse                       1.53 | 21.81         2
2  Session Connect and Disconnect   1.48 | 21.17         1
3  Top SQL Statements               .47 | 6.64           1
4  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations  .39 | 5.54           1
5  Undersized SGA                   .14 | 2.04           1
6  PL/SQL Execution                 .08 | 1.1            3


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.53 active sessions, 21.81% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.53 active sessions, 21.81% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.53 active sessions, 21.81% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.48 active sessions, 21.17% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.48 active sessions, 21.17% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .47 active sessions, 6.64% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .47 active sessions, 6.64% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 8% for SQL execution,
      29% for parsing, 63% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .39 active sessions, 5.54% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .39 active sessions, 5.54% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .68 active sessions, 9.71% of total activity.


Finding 5: Undersized SGA
Impact is .14 active sessions, 2.04% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "184320 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .02 active sessions, .24% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      195840 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .68 active sessions, 9.71% of total activity.


Finding 6: PL/SQL Execution
Impact is .08 active sessions, 1.1% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
PL/SQL execution consumed significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .03 active sessions, .46% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Tune the entry point PL/SQL "SAMATA.PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV" of type
      "PACKAGE" and ID 55287425. Refer to the PL/SQL documentation for
      addition information.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .03 active sessions, .37% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Tune the entry point PL/SQL "CHOSOL.PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV" of type
      "PACKAGE" and ID 20329378. Refer to the PL/SQL documentation for
      addition information.

   Recommendation 3: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .02 active sessions, .27% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Tune the entry point PL/SQL
      "JANTANSP.PKG_CBVER02_FRDRTGSFL.READ_FILES_PARTICULAR" of type "PACKAGE"
      and ID 17861335. Refer to the PL/SQL documentation for addition
      information.

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.22 active sessions, 19.79% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.22 active sessions, 19.79% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.19 active sessions, 19.33% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.19 active sessions, 19.33% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.19 active sessions, 19.33% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.

settings and optimizer parameters.
